newsitem.title: JAPAN: India to consider economic policy changes.
newsitem.headline: India to consider economic policy changes.

text.p: India, encouraged by its success in getting its recent budget approved by a fractured multi-party coalition, is ready for more economic policy changes, Finance Minister Palaniappan Chidambaram said on Sunday..

"The budget has been passed and it is a good sign. There are differences but overriding the differences, we have been able to reconcile it" Chidambaram told Reuters Financial Television in an interview..

"We are also looking at other aspects of economic policy like bringing down interest rates, expanding credit, putting money into infrastrucutre ... I think we are dealing with both supply side as well as demand side," he said..
Chidambaram, who is in this southern Japanese city to attend the Asian Development Bank's annual meeting, has been widely praised for a reform-oriented budget that was recently passed by Parliament..
"We've cut the deficit rate by a percent. We've talked banks into lowering their lending rates. It was 18 to 18.5 percent when I first took over last June," Chidambaram said.
"I think all these steps are to stimulate economic activity," he said.
Prime lending rates are now around 16 percent.
The country's foreign exchange reserves were stronger than expected, causing the rupee to strengthen and the government to look for ways to use it.
"We have to find ways and means to use these reserves which means we will have to liberalise imports. More capital goods imports would be good," Chidambaram said..
Exports had suffered last year with growth in dollar terms falling to just four percent.

"Several key sectors turned sluggish unexpectedly. We have to do micro-management to encourage exports in these sectors. We cannot do with an export growth rate of four percent. We need at least 15 percent," Chidambaram said..

Asked to comment on the view of some analysts that the rupee was overvalued and should be weakened, Chidambaram said: "No, I do not think we should induce a depreciation just to boost someone's confidence. Once you say the rupee will find its level in the market, then you must leave it to the market.".

On the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) stance on the rupee, Chidambaram said: "The RBI is not intervening indiscriminately. Within a band it allows the rupee to fluctuate and it's only when it goes beyond the band does the RBI intervene.".
"Only if it becomes volatile, then the bank should intervene. "Today I think the rupee has found its level and moves within a band," he said..
Chidambaram said one issue on which the government needed to act quickly was the large subsidies given to the oil sector.
Cutting the subsidies would mean raising domestic fuel prices and that is a politically sensitive issue..
The options would be to raise domestic prices along with cutting import duties on crude oil and petroleum products..
But there again it is a tough choice..

"It is difficult to lower import duties right now because the budget assumed a certain amount of revenue. Now if there are compensatroy duties elsewhere, then one can think of lowering duties ... I think we should go for a mix of options," Chidambaram said.
